source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះសណ្តែកបាយ" (Mung Bean Cultivation Techniques handbook), Kingdom of Cambodia, MAFF, published by the Department of Agricultural Extension. Reference list on the closing page cites additional 2003-dated MAFF/agricultural-extension source booklets on mung bean varieties, seed production, and pest management, plus several international references (Plant Resources of South-East Asia Vol. I, 1992; Talekar & Skinner, Field Guide to Insect Pests of Tropical Asia, 1995; Nelson, Insect Pests of Vegetables, Philippines, 1969; Mung Bean Adaptation Trial, Kbalkoh Station 1996-2000, CLV Network; and a 1991 Bangkok workshop proceedings on Yellow Mosaic Virus). No elibrary.maff.gov.kh URL is visible on the scanned pages provided, so none is given here. Uploaded as a 38-page scanned PDF; no embedded text layer, all content read visually from page images. This is Source C for crop/mung_bean in this knowledge base (Sources A-B were processed in Batch 42).
text: Mung bean (ដំណាំសណ្តែកបាយ, Mung Bean) is described as a popular rotation crop with good economic returns, grown widely by both smallholder farmers and commercial producers for its versatility: the crop can be processed into a range of food and feed products, and consumer demand both domestically and internationally has grown because of its favorable nutrient content. The source traces the crop's origins to India, from where cultivation spread according to soil type and climate suitability. Botanically the crop belongs to family Leguminosae, and the source describes two related legume types together in this section: (1) an erect, small dark-seeded type with pods pointing upward, given the scientific name Vigna mungo L. and the common name "Black gram," said to have originated in cooler-climate countries and to be common in Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and India before later spreading to the Americas and Africa; and (2) a round-grained type with grey-toned skin when ripe, scientific name Vigna radiata L., common names "Mung bean," "Green gram," or "Golden gram."
caveat: Source-terminology flag, not resolved: the source's own text labels this second type (Vigna radiata, i.e. true mung bean/green gram) with the Khmer name សណ្តែកប្រេង in its running text, which conflicts with this knowledge base's established convention (set in Batch 42) that សណ្តែកប្រេង = black gram = Vigna mungo. This file uses product="mung_bean" based on the scientific name Vigna radiata and the English common names given (Mung bean/Green gram/Golden gram), consistent with prior-batch product tagging, but the Khmer-name overlap between the two species as printed in this particular source is reported here rather than silently corrected.
